description:
## Goal

Replace `DispatchDemand::Whole` with an exact typed description of the semantic axes a dispatch question reads. Activation keys must retain only those axes, including after demand is pulled backward through the typed path relation established by `fz-kdt.214`.

## Current defect

`Whole` means “retain the complete Ty” for literal, type, map, bitstring, and guard questions. It therefore preserves unrelated denotational axes and defeats convergence collapse. After forwarding became transitive, this over-broad value propagates into callers: the recorded corpus signal was 344 rows across 174 functions gaining a forwarding-introduced `Whole`, with no behavior mover but needless activation distinctions and weakened recursion bounds.

It is also too coarse for the new path relation. A known map-key-presence question depends on the key’s presence, not a reconstructed field value; a bitstring-kind question need not retain unrelated content; an atom literal question need not retain list, tuple, callable, or numeric alternatives.

## Prerequisite and ordering

`fz-kdt.214` first publishes one exact normalized input-flow relation with typed structural paths. This ticket then defines the final question/demand domain and its pullback through those paths. Only afterward does `fz-kdt.213` replace cone solving with ordinary reactive formulas, so the formulas and convergence proof are written once over the final domain. `fz-kdt.165` remains responsible for callable identity as a separate fourth atomic dimension.

## Correct model

- A dispatch demand is an immutable join-semilattice of typed semantic questions, not a “keep everything” escape hatch.
- Literal equality retains only the discriminant axis needed by that literal.
- Type, tuple, list, map, struct, bitstring, numeric, and guard predicates name only the axes they inspect.
- Map presence and map value/content are distinct. Known typed keys remain exact; dynamic keys use an explicit conservative any-key axis.
- Bitstring kind/shape and bitstring content are distinct wherever the dispatch machinery distinguishes them.
- Pullback through `InputFlow` uses its source/destination prefix relation. Projection and reconstruction preserve only the demanded subaxis.
- Join is commutative, associative, idempotent, and finite-height; no axis derives identity from display strings, canonical Ty text, or raw interner order.
- Recursive collapse retains demanded axes and collapses every orthogonal axis, restoring the finite convergence argument.

## TDD

- Atom literal dispatch retains the atom discriminant while collapsing adjacent list, tuple, callable, numeric, map, and bitstring alternatives.
- Numeric literal/type/guard questions retain exactly the numeric distinctions they read.
- Tuple and list shape/field demands pull backward through direct, projected, reconstructed, and Tail/Head paths without retaining sibling fields.
- Known map-key presence does not demand the field value; known field-value questions do; reconstructed maps retain only the relevant typed key.
- Dynamic map access remains conservative without turning unrelated non-map axes into authority.
- Bitstring kind/shape tests do not retain unrelated content axes.
- Transitive forwarding produces the same exact axis demand at every caller.
- Self and mutual recursion converge independent of order with a finite bound.
- The recorded 344 over-broad forwarded rows fall or are causally accounted for; existing bought distinctions and every semantic result remain.

## Required deletion

Delete `DispatchDemand::Whole`, its verbatim-Ty collapse branch, stale “whole value” documentation, and every fallback that silently widens an expressible typed question. Delete `.214`'s temporary SCC structural budget, `N_K` normalizer, and policy-specific recursive-over-approximation tests once the final finite-height question axes make them unnecessary. Do not add a parallel mask, renderer-based classifier, compatibility conversion, or second path walker.

## Acceptance

- Every production dispatch predicate maps to a typed question-axis value.
- Every `InputFlow` path selector has one defined demand-pullback rule.
- Equal demand reproduction preserves allocation/generation and wakes nobody.
- No relevant semantic distinction is lost; no orthogonal Ty axis is retained merely because the old lattice could not express the question.
- Corpus activation/work movement is measured causally and is no worse without a named semantic reason.
- Focused laws, full keying and recursion tests, all three target doors, full serial library and fixture matrix, cross-process determinism, formatting, documentation checks, `cargo check`, and strict clippy pass.
- A fresh ticket-scoped cold adversarial review accepts the final diff before its one commit and close.

comments.text: fz-kdt.183 landed (2e0bb2706): DispatchDemand::Whole returns ty verbatim (no collapse), and forwarding now hands a Whole UP from a callee that pattern-matches a literal: grow/2's accumulator loses its collapse, 1 -> 2 keys, identical at union widths 3/6/9/12 (bounded, measured). 344 rows / 174 functions gain a forwarding-introduced Whole. fz-y6w's termination argument does not cover such a slot; stated in convergence_collapse's doc, type-specialization.md and addressed-arrow.md. The one divergent shape found (self-nesting accumulator) hangs at base with no forwarding at all -- fz-kdt.177's class, not this.

title: Make InputDemand express exact semantic question axes
